subtopic: Reading 91.1 Guidance for Standards I(A) and I(B)
new_question_en: David Martin, CFA, recently joined Arc Financial as a portfolio manager of an emerging markets mutual fund. For the past three years, he managed an emerging markets mutual fund for Landmark Investments. Upon Martin's arrival, Arc Financial announces to existing and prospective clients, "While at Landmark Investments, Martin was the senior portfolio manager of Alpha Emerging Markets Fund. In Martin's three years as manager, this fund outperformed its benchmark each year, as documented in recent reports by Landmark." Does this statement violate the CFA Institute Standard of Professional Conduct related to performance presentation?
new_option_a: No.
new_option_b: Yes, because the Standards prohibit showing past performance at a prior firm.
new_option_c: Yes, because Arc must present at least five years of Martin’s performance history.

subtopic: Reading 91.1 Guidance for Standards I(A) and I(B)
new_question_en: Shortly after becoming employed by Valco & Co., an investment banking firm, Stan McDowell, CFA, learns that most of Valco's initial public offerings (IPO) are really put in place to profit management via price manipulation of the shares. McDowell observes an illegal act, sanctioned by senior management, in progress and refuses to sign off on his responsibility. Instead, McDowell takes the documentation to his supervisor and tells him he should sign it in his place. This action is:
new_option_a: a suitable reaction, and he is in compliance with the Code and Standards.
new_option_b: a violation of the Code and Standards since he is required not to knowingly participate or assist in such an act.
new_option_c: an overreaction. Senior management's sanctioning of the act absolves McDowell from his ordinary responsibility as a CFA Institute member.

subtopic: Reading 91.1 Guidance for Standards I(A) and I(B)
new_question_en: John Farr, CFA, has accumulated several pieces of nonmaterial nonpublic information about CattleCorp from his contacts with the company. From analysis based on this information, together with public information, Farr concludes that CattleCorp will have unexpectedly low earnings this year. Farr has contacted the company, but they will not confirm his conclusion. According to CFA Institute Standards of Professional Conduct, Farr:
new_option_a: may not trade or make recommendations based on his analysis.
new_option_b: may trade or make recommendations based on his analysis.
new_option_c: may trade or make recommendations based on his analysis only if his company’s compliance officer determines that the nonpublic information he used was not material.

subtopic: Reading 91.1 Guidance for Standards I(A) and I(B)
new_question_en: Denise Weaver, CFA, manages a mutual fund and several pension plans. When Weaver receives a proxy for stock held by the mutual fund, she gives it to Susan Griffith, her administrative assistant, to vote according to the recommendations of the company's management. When the proxy is for a stock held by one of the pension plans, she asks Griffith to send the proxy on to the pension fund's sponsor to vote. Weaver has:
new_option_a: violated the Standards by her policy on mutual fund and pension fund proxies.
new_option_b: violated the Standards by her policy on mutual fund proxies, but not her policy on pension fund proxies.
new_option_c: not violated the Standards with her policies on voting proxies.

subtopic: Reading 91.1 Guidance for Standards I(A) and I(B)
new_question_en: Linda Schultz, CFA, is an investment advisor at Wheaton Investments. Schultz has been employed there for five years, and has never signed a "non-compete" clause. While at Wheaton, Schultz makes preparations to set up her own money management firm. She does not contact any existing clients before leaving Wheaton and does not take any firm records or files. After her resignation becomes effective, Schultz replicates a list of former clients from memory and uses public sources to get their contact information. She then contacts these former clients and solicits their business for her new firm. Has Schultz violated any CFA Institute Standards?
new_option_a: No. Schultz is in compliance with CFA Institute Standards.
new_option_b: Yes. Schultz may not contact clients of her old firm.
new_option_c: Yes. Schultz is permitted to notify clients that she has left her old firm, but she cannot encourage them to come with her to the new firm.

subtopic: Reading 26 Capital Investments and Capital Allocation
new_question_en: Which of the following examples best represents a flexibility option?
new_option_a: In three years, a company can invest $500 million to increase the size of its project by 40%.
new_option_b: In two years, a company can cease operating a factory if the present value of production is negative.
new_option_c: In one year, a company can increase the price of its product by up to 30% if demand rises.

subtopic: Reading 26 Capital Investments and Capital Allocation
new_question_en: Johnson's Jar Lids is deciding whether to begin producing jars. Johnson's pays a consultant $50,000 for market research that concludes Johnson's sales of jar lids will increase by 5% if it also produces jars. In choosing the cash flows to include when evaluating a project to begin producing jars, Johnson's should:
new_option_a: include both the cost of the market research and the effect on the sales of jar lids.
new_option_b: include the cost of the market research and exclude the effect on the sales of jar lids.
new_option_c: exclude the cost of the market research and include the effect on the sales of jar lids.

new_question_en: Which of the following is least likely one of the combinations of the quality of financial reporting and quality of reported earnings along the spectrum of financial report quality?
new_option_a: Reporting is not compliant with GAAP, although reported earnings are sustainable and adequate.
new_option_b: Reporting is not compliant and includes numbers that are fictitious or fraudulent.
new_option_c: Reporting is compliant with GAAP, but the amount of earnings is actively managed to smooth earnings.

new_question_en: On a spectrum for assessing financial reporting quality, which of the following represents the highest quality?
new_option_a: Reporting is compliant with GAAP and decision useful but earnings are not sustainable.
new_option_b: Reporting is compliant with GAAP but reporting choices and estimates are biased.
new_option_c: Reporting is not compliant with GAAP but the numbers presented reflect the company’s actual activities.

new_question_en: If a firm's financial reports are of low quality, can users of the reports assess the quality of the firm's earnings?
new_option_a: No, because low-quality financial reports are not useful for assessing the quality of earnings.
new_option_b: Yes, because users can assess earnings quality independently of financial reporting quality.
new_option_c: Yes, because if financial reports are of low quality, earnings are also of low quality.

new_question_en: In which of the following situations is management most likely to make conservative choices and estimates that reduce the quality of financial reports?
new_option_a: Management’s compensation is closely tied to near-term performance of the firm’s stock.
new_option_b: The firm must meet accounting benchmarks to comply with debt covenants.
new_option_c: Earnings for a period will be higher than analysts’ expectations.

new_question_en: Which of the following conditions is most likely necessary for capital to be allocated to its most valuable uses?
new_option_a: Financial markets are frictionless (i.e., free of taxes or transactions costs).
new_option_b: Investors are well informed about the risk and return of various investments.
new_option_c: There are no barriers to the flow of complete information to the financial markets.

new_question_en: Which of the following statements about securities exchanges is most accurate?
new_option_a: Call markets are markets in which the stock is only traded at specific times.
new_option_b: Continuous markets are markets where trades occur 24 hours per day.
new_option_c: Setting a negotiated price to clear the market is a method used to set the closing price in major continuous markets.

new_question_en: Which of the following statements about securities markets is least accurate?
new_option_a: Characteristics of a well-functioning securities market include: many buyers and sellers, low bid-ask spreads, timely information on price and volume of past transactions, and accurate information on supply and demand.
new_option_b: A limit buy order and a stop buy order are both placed below the current market price.
new_option_c: Secondary markets, such as the over-the-counter (OTC) market, provide liquidity and price continuity.

new_question_en: Which of the following statements regarding margin accounts is most accurate?
new_option_a: Maintenance margin refers to the amount of funds the investor can borrow.
new_option_b: Margin accounts can be used to purchase securities by borrowing part of the purchase price.
new_option_c: The total equity in the margin account cannot fall below the initial margin requirement.

new_question_en: When using margin to invest in equities, which of the following defines initial margin and what level will the margin be brought back to in the event of a margin call? Initial Margin Margin Call Action
new_option_a: minimum amount of equity required of the investor a deposit must be made to bring the margin back to the initial margin
new_option_b: minimum amount of equity required of the investor a deposit must be made to bring the margin back to the maintenance margin
new_option_c: amount of borrowed funds in the transactions a deposit must be made to bring the margin back to the maintenance margin

new_question_en: Which of the following statements about financial intermediaries is most accurate?
new_option_a: Arbitrageurs buy securities with the anticipation that they will be able to sell the securities in the future at higher prices.
new_option_b: Brokers seek out traders that are willing to take the opposite sides of their clients’ orders.
new_option_c: Dealers buy a security in one market and simultaneously sell the same security in a different market.

new_question_en: Which of the following statements regarding primary and secondary markets is least accurate?
new_option_a: New issues of government securities can be sold on the primary market.
new_option_b: Prevailing market prices are determined by primary market transactions and are used in pricing new issues.
new_option_c: Secondary market transactions occur between two investors and do not involve the firm that originally issued the security.

new_question_en: Which of the following statements about primary and secondary markets is least accurate?
new_option_a: A primary market is a market in which new securities are sold.
new_option_b: The proceeds from a sale in the secondary market go to the issuer.
new_option_c: The primary market benefits from the liquidity provided by the secondary market.

subtopic: Reading 18 Capital Flows and the FX Market
new_question_en: Akor is a country that has chosen to use a conventional fixed peg arrangement as the country's exchange rate regime. Under this arrangement, Akor's exchange rate against the currency to which it pegs:
new_option_a: will be equal to the peg rate.
new_option_b: is market-determined.
new_option_c: may fluctuate around the peg rate. CPIF CPID

new_question_en: Brian Bellow, CFA, is a portfolio manager for Progressive Trust Company. Several friends have asked Bellow to review their investment portfolios. On his own time, Bellow examines their portfolios and makes several recommendations. He accepts no compensation from his friends for his investment advice. According to CFA Institute Standards of Professional Conduct, did Bellow violate his duty to Progressive Trust?
new_option_a: No, because Bellow provided no ongoing investment advice.
new_option_b: Yes, because Bellow did not attempt to solicit his friends to become clients of his employer.
new_option_c: No, because Bellow received no compensation for his services.

new_question_en: Jack Salyers, CFA, is considering starting his own firm to compete with his current employer. He takes several actions before turning in his resignation. Which of the following actions least likely violates the Standard concerning loyalty? Salyers:
new_option_a: registers his new firm with the government’s financial regulators.
new_option_b: informs clients he has been serving that he is forming a new firm and offers them a discount on fees if they move their accounts to the new firm.
new_option_c: copies computer models he has been using to form a reasonable basis for his investment recommendations.

new_question_en: Which of the following statements regarding employee/employer relationships is NOT correct?
new_option_a: A written contract may or may not exist between employer and employee.
new_option_b: An employee is someone in the service of another.
new_option_c: There must be monetary compensation for an employer/employee relationship to exist.

new_question_en: Jill Marsh, CFA, works for Advisors where she manages various portfolios. Marsh's godfather is an accountant and has done Marsh's tax returns every year as a birthday gift. Marsh's godfather has recently become a client of Advisors and asked specifically for Marsh to manage his account. In order to comply Standard IV(B), Disclosure of Additional Compensation Arrangements, she needs to:
new_option_a: do neither of the actions listed here.
new_option_b: have her godfather cease doing her taxes.
new_option_c: liquidate from her personal portfolio any stocks her godfather owns and verbally tell her supervisor about the tax services.

new_question_en: John Hill, CFA, has been working for Advisors, Inc., for eight years. Hill is about to start his own money management business and has given his two weeks' notice of his resignation from Advisors. A few days before his resignation takes effect, Rod Bright, a former client of Advisors, calls Hill at his home about his new firm. Bright says that he is very happy that Hill is leaving Advisors because now he and Hill can resume a professional relationship. Bright says that he would never become a client of Advisors again. Hill promises to call Bright back after he has left Advisors but takes no further action. Hill does not tell Advisors about the call. Hill has most likely:
new_option_a: violated the Standard concerning loyalty to employer.
new_option_b: violated the Standard concerning disclosure of conflicts.
new_option_c: not violated the Standards.

new_question_en: Sue Parsons, CFA, works full-time as an investment advisor for the Malloy Group, an asset management firm. Parsons wants to engage in independent practice in which she would advise individual clients on their portfolios. She would conduct these investment activities only on weekends. She is currently only in the preparation stage and has not started independent practice yet. The Standard concerning loyalty:
new_option_a: does not require Parsons to notify Malloy of preparing an independent practice.
new_option_b: requires Parsons to obtain consent from both Malloy and the persons from whom she will engage in independent practice.
new_option_c: requires Parsons to notify Malloy that she is preparing to engage in independent practice.

new_question_en: When a CFA Institute member who is presently employed by a firm undertakes any independent practice, he must do all of the following EXCEPT:
new_option_a: disclose the expected duration of the services to be rendered.
new_option_b: remand a percentage (to be determined by the employee and employer) of the income earned back to the employer.
new_option_c: secure permission from the employer.

new_question_en: Edwin McNeill, CFA, is a senior trader for Grey Securities. In his monthly review of his team's activity, McNeill notices a series of suspicious trades by one of the traders. McNeill consults his manager, who agrees that these trades are a potential violation. McNeill informs the trader that her duties will be restricted while these trades are being investigated and refers the matter to Grey's compliance officer for further action. McNeill has:
new_option_a: not violated the Standards.
new_option_b: violated Standard IV(C) Responsibilities of Supervisors by failing to prevent a potential violation.
new_option_c: violated Standard IV(C) Responsibilities of Supervisors by restricting the trader’s duties before the investigation is completed.

new_question_en: Which of the following statements about hypothesis testing is least accurate?
new_option_a: If the alternative hypothesis is Ha: µ > µ0, a two-tailed test is appropriate.
new_option_b: A Type II error is failing to reject a false null hypothesis.
new_option_c: The null hypothesis is a statement about the value of a population parameter.

new_question_en: A data analyst compares the P/E ratios for two companies over a period of 20 years and calculates a two-tailed F-statistic that exceeds the critical F-statistic value. As a result of her findings, she will:
new_option_a: not reject the null hypothesis that the P/E ratio variances between the two companies are significantly different.
new_option_b: reject the null hypothesis that the P/E ratio variances between the two companies are significantly different.
new_option_c: reject the null hypothesis that the P/E ratio variances between the two companies are not significantly different.

new_question_en: An analyst calculates that the mean of a sample of 200 observations is 5. The analyst wants to determine whether the calculated mean, which has a standard error of the sample statistic of 1, is significantly different from 7 at the 5% level of significance. Which of the following statements is least accurate?:
new_option_a: The null hypothesis would be: H0: mean = 7.
new_option_b: The alternative hypothesis would be Ha: mean > 7.
new_option_c: The mean observation is significantly different from 7, because the calculated Z- statistic is less than the critical Z-statistic.

new_question_en: A survey is taken to determine whether the average starting salaries of CFA charterholders is equal to or greater than $58,500 per year. What is the test statistic given a sample of 175 CFA charterholders with a mean starting salary of $67,000 and a standard deviation of $5,200?
Which of the following statements about hypothesis testing is most accurate?
new_option_a: The probability of a Type I error is equal to the significance level of the test.
new_option_b: The power of a test is one minus the probability of a Type I error.
new_option_c: If you can disprove the null hypothesis, then you have proven the alternative hypothesis.

new_question_en: Which of the following statements about hypothesis testing is least accurate?
new_option_a: A Type I error is the probability of rejecting the null hypothesis when the null hypothesis is false.
new_option_b: The significance level is the probability of making a Type I error.
new_option_c: A Type II error is the probability of failing to reject a null hypothesis that is not true.

new_question_en: Which of the following statements about hypothesis testing is most accurate?
new_option_a: A Type I error is rejecting the null hypothesis when it is true, and a Type II error is rejecting the alternative hypothesis when it is true.
new_option_b: A hypothesis that the population mean is less than or equal to 5 should be rejected when the critical Z-statistic is greater than the sample Z-statistic.
new_option_c: A hypothesized mean of 3, a sample mean of 6, and a standard error of the sampling means of 2 give a sample Z-statistic of 1.5.

subtopic: Reading 3 Statistical Measures of Asset Returns
new_question_en: A portfolio's monthly returns follow a distribution with a kurtosis measure of 4.2. Relative to a portfolio with normally distributed returns, this portfolio has a:
new_option_a: higher probability of extreme upside returns and higher chance of extreme downside returns.
new_option_b: lower probability of extreme upside returns and higher chance of extreme downside returns.
new_option_c: higher probability of extreme upside returns and lower chance of extreme downside returns.

new_question_en: Which of the following is least accurate regarding product development and marketing for firms under monopolistic competition?
new_option_a: Brand names can provide consumers with information regarding the quality of firm’s products.
new_option_b: Firms that bring new and innovative products to the market face relatively more elastic demand curves than their competitors.
new_option_c: Relative to other types of competition, product innovation is critical to the pursuit of economic profits.

subtopic: Reading 57 The Term Structure of Interest Rates- Spot, Par, and Forward Curves
new_question_en: = + + + + = 19.80 + 19.51 + 19.13 + 18.48 + 879.86 = $956.78 976 −956.78 = $19.22 20 1.01 20 1.01252 20 1.0153 20 1.024 1020 1.035 Which of the following statements regarding zero-coupon bonds and spot interest rates is CORRECT?
new_option_a: If the yield to maturity on a 2-year zero coupon bond is 6%, then the 2-year spot rate is 3%.
new_option_b: Price appreciation creates all of the zero-coupon bond's return.
new_option_c: Spot interest rates will never vary across the term structure.

subtopic: Reading 57 The Term Structure of Interest Rates- Spot, Par, and Forward Curves
new_question_en: Current spot rates are as follows: 1-Year: 6.5% 2-Year: 7.0% 3-Year: 9.2% Which of the following statements is most accurate?
new_option_a: For a 3-year annual pay coupon bond, all cash flows can be discounted at 9.2% to find the bond's arbitrage-free value.
new_option_b: The yield to maturity for 3-year annual pay coupon bond can be found by taking the geometric average of the 3 spot rates.
new_option_c: For a 3-year annual pay coupon bond, the first coupon can be discounted at 6.5%, the second coupon can be discounted at 7.0%, and the third coupon plus maturity value can be discounted at 9.2% to find the bond's arbitrage-free value.

subtopic: Reading 57 The Term Structure of Interest Rates- Spot, Par, and Forward Curves
new_question_en: An investor wants to take advantage of the 5-year spot rate, currently at a level of 4.0%. Unfortunately, the investor just invested all of his funds in a 2-year bond with a yield of 3.2%. The investor contacts his broker, who tells him that in two years he can purchase a 3-year bond and end up with the same return currently offered on the 5-year bond. What 3-year forward rate beginning two years from now will allow the investor to earn a return equivalent to the 5-year spot rate?
A company with a moderate approach to working capital management would most likely fund:
new_option_a: permanent current assets using long-term funds, and fund seasonal current assets using short-term funds.
new_option_b: both permanent and seasonal current assets using short-term funds.
new_option_c: permanent current assets using short-term funds, and fund seasonal current assets using long-term funds.

new_question_en: Which of the following scenarios is most consistent with a conservative approach to working capital management?
new_option_a: A company funds its rent expense using short-term debt.
new_option_b: A company holds significantly higher amounts of long-term assets than short- term assets.
new_option_c: A company funds its inventory needs using long-term debt.

new_question_en: Which of the following most accurately represents the cash conversion cycle?
new_option_a: average days of receivables + average days of inventory + average days of payables.
new_option_b: average days of payables + average days of inventory – average days of receivables.
new_option_c: average days of receivables + average days of inventory – average days of payables.

new_question_en: A company that reports under U.S. GAAP and changes its inventory cost assumption from weighted average cost to last-in first-out is required to apply this change in accounting principle:
new_option_a: prospectively, and explain the reasons for the change in the financial statement disclosures.
new_option_b: retrospectively, and disclose the new cost flow method being used.
new_option_c: retrospectively, and explain the reasons for the change in the financial statement disclosures.

new_question_en: During periods of rising prices and stable or growing inventories, the most informative inventory accounting method for income statement purposes is:
new_option_a: FIFO because it allocates historical prices to cost of good sold (COGS) and provides a better measure of current income.
new_option_b: LIFO because it allocates current prices to cost of good sold (COGS) and provides a better measure of current income.
new_option_c: weighted average because it allocates average prices to cost of good sold (COGS) and provides a better measure of current income.

new_question_en: Tim Rogers is senior equity analyst with White Capital LLP. While analyzing the inventory disclosures of Drako Toys Inc., a toy manufacturer based in Cleveland, Ohio, Rogers concludes that Drako is expected to see above-average sales growth over the next three years. Which of the following disclosures would most likely support Rogers's conclusion?
new_option_a: Finished goods inventory growing faster than sales in the last two years.
new_option_b: Increase in raw-materials and work-in-progress inventory and corresponding decline in finished goods inventory over the last two years.
new_option_c: Increase in finished goods inventory and corresponding decline in raw-materials and work-in-progress inventory over the last two years.

new_question_en: During periods of decreasing prices, a firm using a periodic inventory system will report higher gross profit if its inventory cost assumption is:
new_option_a: FIFO because during periods of decreasing prices, COGS will be lower, resulting in a higher gross profit.
new_option_b: FIFO because during periods of decreasing prices, COGS will be higher, resulting in a higher gross profit.
new_option_c: LIFO because during periods of decreasing prices, COGS will be lower, resulting in a higher gross profit.

subtopic: Reading 76 Option Replication Using PutCall Parity
new_question_en: A synthetic European call option includes a short position in:
new_option_a: the underlying asset.
new_option_b: a risk-free bond.
new_option_c: a European put option.

subtopic: Reading 76 Option Replication Using PutCall Parity
new_question_en: Using put-call parity, it can be shown that a synthetic European put can be created by a portfolio that is:
new_option_a: short the stock, long the call, and long a pure discount bond that pays the exercise price at option expiration.
new_option_b: short the stock, long the call, and short a pure discount bond that pays the exercise price at option expiration.
new_option_c: long the stock, short the call, and short a pure discount bond that pays the exercise price at option expiration.

new_question_en: Jimmy Deininger, CFA, manages several client portfolios. One of his clients offers him use of a cabin in a vacation spot because the client's investment results under Deininger's management have exceeded the client's goals. Deininger discloses the gift to his employer. With reference to the Standards of Practice, Deininger:
new_option_a: has complied with the Standards and may accept the gift.
new_option_b: is not permitted to accept the gift because he does not have permission from his employer.
new_option_c: has appropriately disclosed the gift to his supervisor, but must also disclose it to his other clients.

new_question_en: A manufacturing plant exhibits diseconomies of scale if long-run average cost (LRAC) is:
new_option_a: decreasing as output increases, and the plant is at its minimum efficient scale if LRAC is at its lowest level.
new_option_b: decreasing as output increases, and the plant is at its minimum efficient scale if LRAC is decreasing over the entire range of output.
new_option_c: increasing as output increases, and the plant is at its minimum efficient scale if LRAC is at its lowest level.

new_question_en: Dot Corporation uses accelerated depreciation for tax purposes and straight-line depreciation for financial reporting. The company has a large cash position which is invested in tax-free municipal bonds. With regard to Dot's financial statements and tax reporting:
new_option_a: both the interest income and the depreciation method will necessitate the use of a valuation allowance account.
new_option_b: the interest income will result in a deferred tax asset and the depreciation method will result in a deferred tax liability.
new_option_c: the depreciation expense causes a temporary difference between income tax expense and taxes payable, and the interest income creates a permanent difference.

new_question_en: Aros Funds manages a family of mutual funds and employs a team of fundamental analysts, who research firms by analyzing financial statements and SEC filings. Under which form(s) of the efficient market hypothesis (EMH) would Aros Funds have the potential to achieve positive risk-adjusted returns consistently using fundamental analysis?
new_option_a: Weak form only.
new_option_b: Semistrong form and weak form.
new_option_c: No form of the EMH is consistent with earning positive risk-adjusted returns using fundamental analysis.

new_question_en: An investor buys a non-dividend paying stock for $100 at the beginning of the year with 50% initial margin. At the end of the year, the stock price is $95. Deflation of 2% occurred during the year. Which of the following return measures for this investment will be greatest?
new_option_a: Real return.
new_option_b: Nominal return.
new_option_c: Leveraged return.

new_question_en: Andrew Pollard, CFA, overhears two executives from a multinational oil company discussing an unexpectedly large earnings increase the company is preparing to announce the following morning. When Pollard gets home that evening, he places an order to buy shares in this oil company. Which of the following best describes this situation?
new_option_a: Pollard violated the Standards by acting on material nonpublic information.
new_option_b: There is no violation of CFA Institute Standards since this was simply an overheard conversation.
new_option_c: Pollard violated CFA Institute Standards by not contacting counsel for advice before placing the trade.

new_question_en: Ron Brenner, CFA, manages portfolios for individuals. One of his clients, John Perlman, offers Brenner several inducements above those provided by his employer to motivate superior future performance in managing his portfolio. Brenner notifies his manager via e-mail about the terms of this offer, and his employer grants permission. According to the Standard on additional compensation arrangements, Brenner:
new_option_a: must notify “all parties involved,” which includes his other clients.
new_option_b: has taken all the actions required to accept the arrangement.
new_option_c: should decline this arrangement because it could cause partiality in the handling of other client accounts.

new_question_en: Thomas Baker recently passed the Level III CFA examination. Baker is reviewing a draft of the firm's marketing material to be distributed after he receives his CFA charter. One passage reads, "Baker passed all three Levels of the CFA exam on his first attempts in three consecutive years." Is this statement in compliance with CFA Institute Standards?
new_option_a: Yes, as long as it is a statement of fact.
new_option_b: No, because it implies that Baker has superior ability.
new_option_c: No, because Members or Candidates who passed the exams on their first attempts may not differentiate themselves from those who did not.

new_question_en: An analyst has found an investment with what appears to be a great return-to-risk ratio. The analyst double-checks the data for accuracy, keeps careful records, and is careful to not make any misrepresentations as he simultaneously sends an e-mail to all his clients with a "buy" recommendation. According to Standard V(A), Diligence and Reasonable Basis, the analyst has:
new_option_a: fulfilled all obligations.
new_option_b: violated the Standard by communicating the recommendation via e-mail.
new_option_c: violated the Standard if he does not verify whether the investment is appropriate for all the clients.

subtopic: Reading 90 Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct
new_question_en: According to the Code of Ethics, which of the following statements is NOT correct? CFA Institute members are required to:
new_option_a: comply with the CFA Institute Global Investment Performance Standards.
new_option_b: maintain and improve their competence and strive to maintain the competence of others in the profession.
new_option_c: use reasonable care and exercise independent professional judgment.

subtopic: Reading 90 Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct
new_question_en: Recommended procedures to comply with the Standard related to fair dealing are most likely to include:
new_option_a: requiring investment committee approval for all recommendation changes.
new_option_b: simultaneously informing all investment representatives in the firm about pending recommendation changes.
new_option_c: publishing personnel guidelines for pre-dissemination that prohibit those who know about a pending recommendation from discussing or acting on it.

subtopic: Reading 55 Yield and Yield Spread Measures for Fixed-Rate Bonds
new_question_en: Which of the following is the most accurate statement about stated and effective annual interest rates?
new_option_a: The stated rate adjusts for the frequency of compounding.
new_option_b: The stated annual interest rate is used to find the effective annual rate.
new_option_c: So long as interest is compounded more than once a year, the stated annual rate will always be more than the effective rate.

subtopic: Reading 55 Yield and Yield Spread Measures for Fixed-Rate Bonds
new_question_en: If a callable bond has an option-adjusted spread (OAS) of 75 basis points, this most likely suggests:
new_option_a: the bond has a zero-volatility spread greater than 75 basis points.
new_option_b: the 75 basis points represent the investor’s compensation for credit risk, liquidity risk, and volatility risk.
new_option_c: the implied cost of the call option is the bond’s nominal spread minus 75 basis points.

subtopic: Reading 55 Yield and Yield Spread Measures for Fixed-Rate Bonds
new_question_en: Bond X is a noncallable corporate bond maturing in ten years. Bond Y is also a corporate bond maturing in ten years, but Bond Y is callable at any time beginning three years from now. Both bonds carry a credit rating of AA. Based on this information:
new_option_a: Bond Y will have a higher zero-volatility spread than Bond X.
new_option_b: The option adjusted spread of Bond Y will be greater than its zero-volatility spread.
new_option_c: The zero-volatility spread of Bond X will be greater than its option-adjusted spread.

subtopic: Reading 55 Yield and Yield Spread Measures for Fixed-Rate Bonds
new_question_en: The zero volatility spread (Z-spread) is the spread that:
new_option_a: is added to each spot rate on the government yield curve that will cause the present value of the bond's cash flows to equal its market price.
new_option_b: is added to the yield to maturity of a similar maturity government bond to equal the yield to maturity of the risky bond.
new_option_c: results when the cost of the call option in percent is subtracted from the option adjusted spread.

subtopic: Reading 50 Fixed-Income Cash Flows and Types
new_question_en: Which of the following statements regarding a sinking fund provision is most accurate?
new_option_a: It permits the issuer to retire more than the stipulated amount if they choose.
new_option_b: It requires that the issuer retire a portion of the principal through a series of principal payments over the life of the bond.
new_option_c: It requires that the issuer set aside money based on a predefined schedule to accumulate the cash to retire the bonds at maturity.

subtopic: Reading 50 Fixed-Income Cash Flows and Types
new_question_en: Which of the following issues is most accurately described as a eurobond?
new_option_a: Brazilian firm’s U.S. dollar-denominated bonds sold to investors in Canada.
new_option_b: European Union firm’s Japanese yen-denominated bonds sold to investors in Japan.
new_option_c: South Korean firm’s euro-denominated bonds sold to investors in the European Union.

subtopic: Reading 50 Fixed-Income Cash Flows and Types
new_question_en: Which of the following statements about the call feature of a bond is most accurate? An embedded call option:
new_option_a: stipulates whether and under what circumstances the issuer can redeem the bond prior to maturity.
new_option_b: stipulates whether and under what circumstances the bondholders can request an earlier repayment of the principal amount prior to maturity.
new_option_c: describes the maturity date of the bond.

subtopic: Reading 2 The Time Value of Money in Finance
new_question_en: An investor is choosing between two possible investments. Both have identical future cash flows in all situations, but the investor notices a slight discrepancy in price between the two. What action will this investor take based on the no-arbitrage principle?
new_option_a: Wait for the prices to further diverge, then sell the higher-priced investment.
new_option_b: Do nothing, as there cannot be a price divergence based on the rule.
new_option_c: Act quickly by buying the lower-priced investment, as the prices will quickly converge.

subtopic: Reading 58 Interest Rate Risk and Return
new_question_en: Annual Macaulay duration is least accurately interpreted as the:
new_option_a: approximate percentage change in a bond’s value for a 1% change in its yield to maturity.
new_option_b: investment horizon at which a bond’s market price risk and reinvestment risk exactly offset.
new_option_c: weighted average number of years until a bond’s cash flows are scheduled to be paid.

subtopic: Reading 58 Interest Rate Risk and Return
new_question_en: If the yield to maturity on a bond decreases after purchase but before the first coupon date and the bond is held to maturity, reinvestment risk is:
new_option_a: less than price risk and the realized yield will be lower than the YTM at purchase.
new_option_b: greater than price risk and the realized yield will be lower than the YTM at purchase.
new_option_c: less than price risk and the realized yield will be higher than the YTM at purchase.

subtopic: Reading 69 Forward Commitment and Contingent Claim Features and Instruments
new_question_en: If the margin balance in a futures account with a long position goes below the maintenance margin amount:
new_option_a: a deposit is required to return the account margin to the initial margin level.
new_option_b: a margin deposit equal to the maintenance margin is required within two business days.
new_option_c: a deposit is required which will bring the account to the maintenance margin level.

subtopic: Reading 69 Forward Commitment and Contingent Claim Features and Instruments

new_option_a: call holder will exercise (at expiration) if the exercise price exceeds the stock price.
new_option_b: breakeven point for the buyer is the exercise price plus the option premium.

new_question_en: Which of the following is least likely an appropriate use of the CFA designation?
new_option_a: Jeremy Salyers, as a CFA charterholder, will outperform the market.
new_option_b: Jeremy Salyers, CFA.
new_option_c: Jeremy Salyers has earned the CFA designation by passing three exams, all on his first attempts.

new_question_en: Prior to the beginning of summer, the government of Japan places a 150 percent tariff on imported chain saws. Assume for this example that this tariff has a significant impact on the supply of chain saws. The government's action:
new_option_a: benefits the Japanese government and domestic producers.
new_option_b: will protect the jobs and high wages of Japanese chain saw industry workers.
new_option_c: is more harmful than if the government had limited the amount of chain saws imported.

subtopic: Reading 60 Yield-Based Bond Convexity and Portfolio Properties
new_question_en: A bond is currently priced at 92.35. If the calculated modified duration is 3.27 and the convexity is 15.74, the expected new price of the bond due to a 50 basis point increase in yields is closest to:

subtopic: Reading 60 Yield-Based Bond Convexity and Portfolio Properties
new_question_en: Adjusting for convexity improves an estimated price change for a bond compared to using duration alone because:
new_option_a: it measures the volatility of non-callable bonds.
new_option_b: the slope of the callable bond price/yield curve is backward bending at high interest rates.
new_option_c: the slope of the price/yield curve is not constant.

subtopic: Reading 60 Yield-Based Bond Convexity and Portfolio Properties
new_question_en: How does the price-yield relationship for a callable bond compare to the same relationship for an option-free bond? The price-yield relationship is best described as exhibiting:
new_option_a: negative convexity at low yields for the callable bond and positive convexity for the option-free bond.
new_option_b: negative convexity for the callable bond and positive convexity for an option- free bond.
new_option_c: the same convexity for both bond types.

subtopic: Reading 60 Yield-Based Bond Convexity and Portfolio Properties
new_question_en: Which of the following is most accurate about a bond with positive convexity?
new_option_a: Positive changes in yield lead to positive changes in price.
new_option_b: Price increases and decreases at a faster rate than the change in yield.
new_option_c: Price increases when yields drop are greater than price decreases when yields rise by the same amount.

subtopic: Reading 91.5 Guidance for Standards III(C), III(D), and III(E)
new_question_en: Paula Munson, CFA, manages a mutual fund with an objective to emphasize income over capital gains. Magic Technologies is a growth stock that pays no dividend, but Republic's research department believes the stock will dramatically outperform the S&P 500 over the next 12 to 18 months. Based on this strong recommendation and believing Magic stock will improve the fund's diversification, Munson adds the stock to her fund's portfolio. Munson has:
new_option_a: violated the Standards by failing to comply with her portfolio’s style mandate.
new_option_b: not violated the Standards because she is making investment decisions in a portfolio context.
new_option_c: violated the Standards by relying on research that she did not perform herself.

new_question_en: Which of the following statements about active and passive asset management is most accurate?
new_option_a: Active management has been gaining market share over time versus passive management.
new_option_b: Passive management’s share of industry revenues is smaller than its share of assets under management.
new_option_c: Active management may use fundamental analysis, technical analysis, or a “smart beta” approach to outperform a chosen benchmark.

new_question_en: Open-end mutual funds differ from closed-end funds in that:
new_option_a: open-end funds stand ready to redeem their shares, while closed-end funds do not.
new_option_b: closed-end funds require active management, while open-end funds do not.
new_option_c: open-end funds issue shares that are then traded in secondary markets, while closed-end funds do not.

subtopic: Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D)
new_question_en: Which of the following is most likely permitted under Standard I(C), Misrepresentation?
new_option_a: Citing quotes attributed to "investment experts" without specific reference.
new_option_b: Including data showing the current government bond yield curve in a report to a client without stating its source.
new_option_c: Using excerpts from reports prepared by others without acknowledgement.

subtopic: Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D)
new_question_en: All of the following violate Standard I(C), Misrepresentation, EXCEPT:
new_option_a: citing quotes attributable to "investment experts" without specific references.
new_option_b: presenting factual information published by recognized statistical reporting services without acknowledgment.
new_option_c: copying a proprietary computerized spreadsheet without seeking authorization from the creators.

new_question_en: Which of the following best describes valuation allowance? Valuation allowance is a reserve:
new_option_a: created when deferred tax assets are greater than deferred tax liabilities.
new_option_b: against deferred tax assets based on the likelihood that those assets will not be realized.
new_option_c: against deferred tax liabilities based on the likelihood that those liabilities will be paid.

new_question_en: Which of the following is most likely to cause a difference between a firm's statutory and effective tax rates?
new_option_a: An increase in the deferred tax asset from the prior period, and no change in the deferred tax liability.
new_option_b: An increase in the actual cash paid to the tax authorities.
new_option_c: An increase in the tax-exempt income earned during the period.

new_question_en: Which of the following statements regarding deferred taxes is NOT correct?
new_option_a: Only those components of deferred tax liabilities that are likely to reverse should be considered a liability.
new_option_b: If deferred tax liabilities are not included in equity, debt-to-equity ratio will be reduced.
new_option_c: If deferred taxes are not expected to reverse in the future then they should be classified as equity.

new_question_en: While evaluating the financial statements of Omega, Inc., the analyst observes that the effective tax rate is 7% less than the statutory rate. The source of this difference is determined to be a tax holiday on a manufacturing plant located in South Africa. This item is most likely to be:
new_option_a: continuous in nature, so the termination date is not relevant.
new_option_b: sporadic in nature, and the analyst should try to identify the termination date and determine if taxes will be payable at that time.
new_option_c: sporadic in nature, but the effect is typically neutralized by higher home country taxes on the repatriated profits.

new_question_en: The stakeholder theory of corporate governance is primarily focused on:
new_option_a: increasing the value a company.
new_option_b: resolving the competing interests of those who manage companies and other groups affected by a company’s actions.
new_option_c: the interests of various stakeholders rather than the interests of shareholders.

new_question_en: Which of the following statements is most accurate regarding a firm that chooses to employ a focus-based competitive strategy?
new_option_a: It is often a hybrid strategy, as it may involve elements of both cost leadership and differentiation.
new_option_b: The appeal is for customers who are willing to pay more for perceived value.
new_option_c: The target is a wide range of customers whose needs may differ considerably.

new_question_en: An analyst covering the reinsurance sector observes that the capital structure of three of the covered firms recently deviated from their targets. That analyst should be most concerned with:
new_option_a: Firm C, whose equity weight increased relative to target given the minimum lot size requirement when it issued new equity.
new_option_b: Firm B, whose debt weight increased relative to target following the issuance of new debt.
new_option_c: Firm A, whose equity weight declined relative to target given a drop in the market value of the firm’s equity.

new_question_en: The notice period for a hedge fund is best described as the period following:
new_option_a: a request for redemption of shares, within which the fund must fulfill the request.
new_option_b: an investment in the fund, during which the investor is not permitted to redeem shares.
new_option_c: the opening of the fund to investors, before the fund is closed to new investors.

subtopic: Reading 9 Parametric and Non-Parametric Tests of Independence
new_question_en: In a test of independence based on contingency table data, degrees of freedom are the:
new_option_a: sum of the number of rows and the number of columns.
new_option_b: product of the number of rows minus one and the number of columns, minus one.
new_option_c: sum of the number of rows and the number of columns, minus two.

subtopic: Reading 9 Parametric and Non-Parametric Tests of Independence
new_question_en: To test a hypothesis that the population correlation coefficient of two variables is equal to zero, an analyst collects a sample of 24 observations and calculates a sample correlation coefficient of 0.37. Can the analyst test this hypothesis using only these two inputs?
new_option_a: Yes.
new_option_b: No, because the sample standard deviations of the two variables are also required.
new_option_c: No, because the sample means of the two variables are also required.

new_question_en: Which of the following statements about an organization's risk tolerance is most accurate?
new_option_a: An organization with low risk tolerance should take steps to reduce each of the risks it identifies.
new_option_b: Risk tolerance is the degree to which an organization is able to bear the various risks that may arise from outside the organization.
new_option_c: The financial strength of an organization is one of the factors it should consider when determining its risk tolerance.

subtopic: Reading 22 Organizational Forms, Corporate Issuer Features, and Ownership
new_question_en: With respect to the various business structures, which of the following statements about income taxes is most accurate?
new_option_a: In a limited partnership, all tax due on profits is paid by the limited partners.
new_option_b: In a general partnership, income is taxed at both the partnership and partner (individual) level.
new_option_c: Under a corporate structure, shareholders have no personal tax liability.

subtopic: Reading 22 Organizational Forms, Corporate Issuer Features, and Ownership
new_question_en: Which of the following statements comparing corporations and general partnerships is most accurate?
new_option_a: Owner liability is only limited under a corporation.
new_option_b: Access to capital is easier under a general partnership, given the less complex business structure.
new_option_c: Both corporations and general partnerships are separate legal entities.

new_question_en: An investor is working with his financial planner to incorporate more fixed-income investments into his portfolio. One of the investor's questions centers on bond tracker funds and whether they use sampling to mirror a fixed-income index construction. The planner's response will most likely be that the tracker fund:
new_option_a: uses sampling to minimize transaction complexity.
new_option_b: does not use sampling because that is more prevalent in equity index tracker funds.
new_option_c: does not use sampling because the universe of fixed-income constituents is low relative to equity.

subtopic: Reading 73 Pricing and Valuation of Futures Contracts
new_question_en: If the price of a forward contract is greater than the price of an identical futures contract, the most likely explanation is that:
new_option_a: the futures contract requires daily settlement and the forward contract does not.
new_option_b: the forward contract is more liquid than the futures contract.
new_option_c: the futures contract is more difficult to exit than the forward contract.

subtopic: Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity
new_question_en: ABC Company leases manufacturing equipment for five years with annual payments of $20,000. The company will return the equipment to the lessor at the end of the lease. The term of the lease is equal to the equipment's useful life. Under U.S. GAAP, the company will:
new_option_a: report the lease as an operating lease.
new_option_b: record a right-of-use asset on the balance sheet.
new_option_c: recognize an amortization expense equal to the principal repayment each period.

subtopic: Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity
new_question_en: Which of the following regarding employer contributions is least likely a required disclosure under IFRS?
new_option_a: Expected employer contributions for the next period for defined benefit plans.
new_option_b: Total employer’s contributions expensed in the income statement for defined contribution plans.
new_option_c: Reasons for changes in employer contributions for defined contribution plans.

subtopic: Reading 86 Basics of Portfolio Planning and Construction
new_question_en: Which of the following statements about risk and return is least accurate?
new_option_a: Return objectives may be stated in absolute terms.
new_option_b: Risk and return may be considered on a mutually exclusive basis.
new_option_c: Specifying investment objectives only in terms of return may expose an investor to inappropriately high levels of risk.

new_question_en: Which of the following statements regarding the distribution of returns used for asset pricing models is most accurate?
new_option_a: Lognormal distribution returns are used because this will allow for negative returns on the assets.
new_option_b: Normal distribution returns are used for asset pricing models because they will only allow the asset price to fall to zero.
new_option_c: Lognormal distribution returns are used for asset pricing models because they will not result in an asset return of less than -100%.

subtopic: Reading 64 Credit Analysis for Corporate Issuers
new_question_en: Structural subordination means that a parent company's debt:
new_option_a: has a higher priority of claims to a subsidiary’s cash flows than the subsidiary’s debt.
new_option_b: has a lower priority of claims to a subsidiary’s cash flows than the subsidiary’s debt.
new_option_c: ranks pari passu with a subsidiary’s debt with respect to the subsidiary’s cash flows.

subtopic: Reading 64 Credit Analysis for Corporate Issuers
new_question_en: Miko Corp. (Miko) is an electronics manufacturer which frequently issues senior unsecured bonds. Miko's largest subsidiary, BluTech Inc. (BluTech), also issues senior unsecured bonds. BluTech's debt covenants prohibit transferring cash to the parent before BluTech's debt obligations are satisfied. Based on this scenario:
new_option_a: Miko’s and BluTech’s bonds would rank pari passu given that the two entities are related, regardless of the restriction.
new_option_b: Miko’s bonds are structurally subordinated to BluTech’s bonds.
new_option_c: BluTech’s bonds are structurally subordinated to Miko’s bonds.

subtopic: Reading 53 Fixed-Income Markets for Government Issuers
new_question_en: Relative to the yields on nonsovereign bonds, sovereign bond yields may be lower because of the:
new_option_a: requirement to distribute them in an auction format.
new_option_b: greater risk associated with their issuers.
new_option_c: regulatory requirements, forcing some financial institutions to hold government debt.

subtopic: Reading 68 Derivative Instrument and Derivative Market Features
new_question_en: Which of the following statements regarding derivatives and/or cash market transactions is most accurate?
new_option_a: Investors can easily gain exposure to risk through derivatives but at a relatively high cost.
new_option_b: Initiating a derivatives position is most likely to have a greater impact on market prices of the underlying, relative to initiating an equivalent position in the underlying through a cash market transaction.
new_option_c: Transaction costs for a derivatives position are often lower than for the equivalent cash market trade.

new_question_en: Discretionary fiscal policy refers to:
new_option_a: buying or selling securities in the open market to influence interest rates.
new_option_b: active decisions regarding spending and taxing to affect economic growth.
new_option_c: government spending programs that counteract the business cycle without the intervention of policymakers.

new_question_en: The crowding-out model implies that a:
new_option_a: budget deficit will increase the real interest rate and thereby retard private investment.
new_option_b: budget surplus will retard aggregate demand and trigger an economic downturn.
new_option_c: budget deficit will stimulate aggregate demand and trigger a multiplier effect which will lead to inflation.

subtopic: Reading 70 Derivative Benefits, Risks, and Issuer and Investor Uses
new_question_en: Which of the following statements regarding the use of derivatives is most accurate?
new_option_a: A portfolio manager can decrease exposure to the risk and return of a market index.
new_option_b: The issuer of a fixed-rate obligation can increase risk exposure by converting to a floating-rate obligation.
new_option_c: A manufacturer can hedge the exchange risk of anticipated receipts or payments.

subtopic: Reading 77 Valuing a Derivative Using a One-Period Binomial Model
new_question_en: An option's value is affected by:
new_option_a: expected probabilities of underlying price increases or decreases only.
new_option_b: actual probabilities of underlying price increases or decreases only.
new_option_c: both actual and expected probabilities of underlying price increases or decreases.

subtopic: Reading 77 Valuing a Derivative Using a One-Period Binomial Model
new_question_en: Which of the following statements regarding risk-neutrality is most accurate?
new_option_a: Risk-neutral pricing requires using expected return to price an option.
new_option_b: Risk-neutral probabilities are determined by investor views on risk and the risk- free rate.
new_option_c: Risk-neutral pricing can be applied to any model that uses future underlying asset price movements.

subtopic: Reading 77 Valuing a Derivative Using a One-Period Binomial Model
new_question_en: We can use the risk-free rate to value an option with a one-period binomial model because:
new_option_a: combining options with the underlying asset in a specific ratio will produce a risk-free future payment.
new_option_b: combining put and call options in specific ratio can produce a risk-free future payment.
new_option_c: options investors are risk-neutral, on average.

subtopic: Reading 77 Valuing a Derivative Using a One-Period Binomial Model
new_question_en: In order to value an option with a one-period binomial model, three things an analyst would need to know are:
new_option_a: the risk-adjusted discount rate, the volatility of the price of the underlying asset, and option exercise price.
new_option_b: the risk-free rate, the volatility of the price of the underlying, and the current asset price.
new_option_c: the probability of an up-move, the option exercise price, and the current asset price.

subtopic: Reading 77 Valuing a Derivative Using a One-Period Binomial Model
new_question_en: One method of valuing a call option with a one-period binomial model involves:
new_option_a: using the probabilities of an up-move and a down-move to get the expected value of the payment at expiration.
new_option_b: discounting the average call value at expiration by the risk-free rate.
new_option_c: finding a combination of the call option and the underlying that will have the same value regardless of the price of the underlying at expiration.

subtopic: Reading 63 Credit Analysis for Government Issuers
new_question_en: Which of the following statements about municipal bonds is least accurate?
new_option_a: A municipal bond guarantee is a form of insurance provided by a third party other than the issuer.
new_option_b: Bonds with municipal bond guarantees are more liquid in the secondary market and generally have lower required yields.
new_option_c: Revenue bonds have lower yields than general obligation bonds because they are backed by specific projects.
